newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ hours worked rises s/adj 2.5 pct in June qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ hours worked rises s/adj 2.5 pct in June qtr.

text.p: The number of hours worked in New Zealand rose a seasonally-adjusted 2.5 percent in the June quarter following a 2.0 percent fall in the March quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand forecast in its June 27 Monetary Policy Statement that the number of hours worked would rise 1.9 percent in the June quarer. Private sector economists had expected a rise of 1.0-1.5 percent.
SNZ said that in annual terms the number of hours worked was up 0.6 percent in the June quarter, following a 2.2 percent annual fall in the March quarter.

Releasing its Household Labour Force Survey, SNZ said the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 6.7 percent in the June quarter from a revised 6.5 percent in the March quarter and 6.0 percent in June 1996.
It was the second consecutive rise in the unemployment rate, SNZ said.

Seasonally adjusted figures showed some 122,000 people were unemployed in the quarter. That was up from 117,000 people in the March quarter, and was the highest level of unemployment since December 1994 when 127,000 people were unemployed.
In the year to June 1997, seasonally adjusted unemployment grew by 14,000 (13.0 percent).

On a seasonally adjusted basis, there were some 1.693 million people employed in the June quarter, a quarterly rise of 0.2 percent. Economists polled by Reuters had on average expected a contraction in June quarter employment growth of 0.15 percent.
SNZ said the rise in employment growth followed two consecutive quarterly falls.
The annual rate of employment growth was 0.4 percent, compared to 1.1 percent annual employment growth in the year to March.
During the quarter growth in part time unemployment of 1.6 percent offset a fall in full time employment of 0.4 percent.
The participation rate in the June quarter was 65.7 percent, up from 65.6 percent in the March quarter and 65.8 percent in the June 1996 quarter.
